$comment: Who RELEASED the weights a provider serves — never who serves them. `gpt-oss-120b` and `gemma-4-31b` are served BY Cerebras, which is why the model lines below name `openai` and `google` and the provider slug appears nowhere in them. Putting the serving provider in the publisher slot would make a model's identity change the day a second provider serves the same weights, and the failover set — one reference, several endpoints — could then never be expressed.

THIS TABLE IS THE HALF OF THE INVENTORY THAT IS OXY'S. ADR 0006 gives model catalogue IDENTITY to Oxy and deployment availability to Relay; the inventory file has to carry both, so neither side owns it outright. It lives here because ADR 0006's 'What crosses the boundary' declares exactly one Oxy→Relay channel — the per-request envelope — and no channel by which a catalogue could publish an inventory. If Oxy ever grows one, this file is what it replaces, and nothing around it moves. See internal/publisher/attribution.go.

IT IS DECLARED, NEVER DERIVED. A provider's own /models endpoint is authoritative about what it SERVES and says nothing about who released it: Cerebras answers `gpt-oss-120b`, not `openai/gpt-oss-120b`. Inferring the publisher from the string would put a claim about somebody else's work into a customer-visible identifier on the strength of a substring, so a model id nobody has attributed is DROPPED from the snapshot with a warning and no reference resolves to it.

PROVENANCE OF THE TWO ENTRIES BELOW: read from the Cerebras API with the account's own key on 2026-08-18. `GET https://api.cerebras.ai/v1/models` returned exactly these two ids and nothing else, and `GET /v1/models/<id>` answered 200 for both while every id outside the list answered 404 `model_not_found`. The publisher attribution — `gpt-oss-120b` to OpenAI, `gemma-4-31b` to Google — is each publisher's own announcement of the weights, not Cerebras's description of them.

NO CREDENTIAL, NO ADDRESS, NO PRICE. A provider slug resolves to an adapter, an address and a key pool in cmd/relay, from the process environment. Adding any of them here would make one process's configuration a global fact.

A NEW ENTRY NEEDS A SOURCE, NOT A GUESS. The cheapest way to add a model is to read the publisher's own release announcement; that is the point. An entry for a provider nobody discovers is warned about at startup, because it is otherwise indistinguishable from a provider that serves nothing.
